content: Milia, also referred to as milk spots or oil seeds, are small, benign cysts filled with keratin. These cysts typically form just beneath the epidermis or, in some cases, on the roof of the mouth. While they are most commonly observed in newborn infants, they can occur in individuals of any age. Milia are frequently found in areas around the nose and eyes, though they may also appear on the genitalia in some cases. In children, these cysts often resolve spontaneously within two to four weeks without requiring any medical intervention. However, in adults, milia may persist and sometimes necessitate removal by a healthcare professional, such as a physician or a cosmetologist. In certain instances, milia can develop as a result of external factors, such as the use of harsh facial cleansers or repeated exposure to heat stress, particularly from hot showers. This is especially true for individuals with sensitive skin, where such triggers can contribute to the formation of these cysts.
